item: The first lemmatisation under any language loads that language's simplemma dictionary: nine languages cost about 4-6 s of CPU once per process and about 625 MiB resident, paid by the first caller (the first GET that resolves a keyword, or the diagnostics keyword selftest); stated limit, not changed
refs: R323; WAL deadline sweep (associations 6.6 s at 60,000 and 300,000 articles, 6.13 s cold encrypted); RC2 selftests profile (9.64 s of 13.25 s); /mnt/project-files/keyword-lane/simplemma-first-load-2026-10-27.md
summary: One root for two measured rows. simplemma's DefaultDictionaryFactory loads a language's dictionary on its first use; src/analytics/queries.py:_resolve_by_lemma (line 158) loops every language in LEMMA_LANGS (nine), so the first keyword-resolving GET (GET /api/insights/associations) pays all nine, and the diagnostics keyword selftest reaches the same loads through lemma.lemmatize -> extract._key_for. Measured on one box, cold process, simplemma 1.2.0: de 1.163 s, pt 1.246, es 0.794, ru 0.669, nl 0.521, it 0.418, fr 0.226, en 0.071, id 0.018 (sum 5.13 s in one run; 4.26 s CPU = 4.27 s wall in another), pure CPU with no I/O wait, a second pass 0.0 s; RSS 19 -> 644 MiB. WAL measured 6.6 s (associations, 60,000 and 300,000 articles, so it does not grow with the corpus) and 6.13 s cold encrypted, RC2 9.64 s of the 13.25 s selftest member on a plain store: slower boxes, same statement. NOT CHANGED: narrowing the loop to fewer languages changes results, because the keywords query at queries.py:201 has no language filter and the ambiguity refusal counts candidates from every language (inferred from the code, not measured on a corpus); running the selftest after a member that loaded the dictionaries only moves the same seconds; a boot-time warm would add the 625 MiB to every process and is rejected (R323). PROPOSAL for the user list: B, a lazy named background load that answers a labelled warming until it is ready.
